Amber CLI 2.0.10 generates applications on Amber `v2.0.0-beta.10`, whose request path uses no regex engine, and installs with Minecart 2025.11.25.9.

- New applications pin Amber by commit: `commit: d291e0930dd22b14a2d10f75a9de063abb0e64e4 # v2.0.0-beta.10`, locked with `checksum: sha256-v2:8d354db3b41625db0362162a34836fe10a8b11a378f3837d34cc6bbcece1cb94`.
- `amber new` accepts the `sha256-v2:` checksums Minecart 2025.11.25.9 records, and still accepts the `git-tree:` checksums an older Minecart records.
- A `shard.lock` written on Windows records different `sha256-v2:` values from one written on macOS or Linux. On Windows, `amber new` checks Amber by its commit.
- `amber-lsp --version` reports the release commit in a Homebrew build.
- Generated auth controllers name their missing-session error, and `amber_cli` itself builds with no warnings on these paths.

Upgrading Minecart can stop an install with a shard in `lib/` that `shard.lock` does not pin. Remove that folder, as the message says. A CI cache that restores `lib/` from an older lock hits this too, so cache `~/.cache/shards` only.

releases.body:
# Amber 2.0.0-beta.10

Amber 2.0.0-beta.10 takes the regex engine out of the request path. A JSON API
built on it links no PCRE2 on stock Crystal, and CI now fails if that changes.

## What changed

- **No PCRE2 in a JSON API.** On stock Crystal 1.22.2, an app with one GET and
  one POST shows no `libpcre2` in `otool -L` or `ldd` and no `pcre2_` symbol in
  `nm`, on macOS and on Linux. `scripts/check_linkage.sh` runs in CI, and its
  control program that uses `Regex` must show PCRE2.
- **Typed route rules (#1442).** Route parameter rules are types, and the router
  uses no regex engine.
- **Fixed patterns became plain code (#1443, #1444).** Amber's internal fixed
  patterns read strings directly, and no pattern uses lookaround.
- **Cookies, form keys, formats and backtraces (#1445).** The `Cookie` header,
  form keys, named schema formats, `String#url?`, backtrace frames and the
  exception page's code coloring use hand-written checks. Each check was compared
  with the pattern it replaced on generated input.
- **A crash removed.** `Validator::Format` with `FormatType::URL` raised
  `Regex::Error` on short crafted input. The new check takes time in proportion
  to the input.
- **One bad cookie no longer fails a request.** Amber leaves that pair out and
  keeps the others.

## Keeping your app free of PCRE2

An app links PCRE2 again when it uses any of these, and it keeps working:

- `pattern:`, `filename_pattern:` or a custom `format:` on a schema field, and
  `validates_pattern` or a custom `validates_format`
- a `Regex` passed to `Pipe::CORS`, `Validator::Pattern` or `Validator::Format`
- Markdown, `strip_tags`, and the other `String` checks such as `email?` and `phone?`
- `request.cookies`; read `cookies` instead
- Grant, whose query code uses `Regex` today
- `Regex` in your own code

## Breaking changes

- A route constraint is a rule, and a `Regex` no longer compiles. Replace
  `{"id" => /\d+/}` with `{"id" => :numeric}`. A rule judges the whole segment,
  so `{"cart" => /\d\d\d/}`, which matched `he110`, becomes
  `NUMERIC.with_length(3)`.
- A `Set-Cookie` header on a request is ignored. Specs that replayed response
  headers as a request must send `Cookie`.
- `Validator::Format::PATTERNS` is removed.
- Backtracer `app_dirs_pattern` is now the prefix list `list_of_app_directories`,
  and `modules_path_pattern` is now the prefix `modules_directory`.
- `Pipe::CORS` copies its origin list when it is built, and `cors.origins` holds
  strings and rule procs. `CORS.new` still accepts `CORS::OriginType`, and now
  also `Array(String)`.
- Phone numbers and the host of a `FormatType::URL` value accept ASCII digits only.
- The schema examples moved to `examples/schema`.

`CHANGELOG.md` has the complete list.

## Upgrading

Use Amber CLI 2.0.10 for new apps. For an existing app, pin the release commit in
`shard.yml`, run `minecart update amber`, and run `amber setup:agent`.

## Pin this release

```
Commit: d291e0930dd22b14a2d10f75a9de063abb0e64e4
Tree: fb4574c6b15b60357abd43ed0a1a8d7a0957e574
Tarball: amber-2.0.0-beta.10.tar.gz (git archive --format=tar.gz --prefix=amber-2.0.0-beta.10/ d291e0930dd22b14a2d10f75a9de063abb0e64e4)
Tarball sha256: 94a8315546063132454f995ea92472bd93ebb5192b1efa8838ed96f3f7aece1c
shard.lock checksum (Minecart 2025.11.25.9 and newer): sha256-v2:8d354db3b41625db0362162a34836fe10a8b11a378f3837d34cc6bbcece1cb94
```


**Mica's lock line.** Minecart 2025.11.25.9 records Mica v0.1.1 as `checksum: sha256-v2:f13de354cf66409ccbc1e975f08b23e230620fc895309d057b7ba79aa07ce4e4`. `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/guides/schema-api.md` in this tag still show the `git-tree:22075f8ddb2d5874bdf260f0e4b00a3927d0515d` that older Minecart records. Both values name the same release. `v2-dev` has the new value.

## Minecart 2025.11.25.9

Hardens `install --frozen` against a hostile dependency:

- Reused copies are checked against their locked source, and any `lib/` entry the lock does not list fails by name.
- A postinstall script that changes another installed copy, adds a `lib/` entry or changes `shard.lock` stops the install by name. The checks and cleanup also run when the script fails.
- A nested install inside a postinstall script resolves from the project's lock, so it cannot overwrite the project's locked copies.
- New lock entries record `sha256-v2:` checksums. Existing `git-tree:` and `sha256:` entries keep verifying.

`docs/compliance-guide.md` lists what these checks cannot see.

Source commit: `ec4ec4d4434a92308f99de11ac907fc8a21e7a79`
Tree: `dd6c0d1cfdfe1c1b78dd515a3117088b31416f2e`
Source archive sha256: `eea3951ec589fcf005517514a5b83d0d6702bd82e5e261ac0bf38d6900204ec2`

Install on macOS or Linux with Homebrew, which builds from this source archive. This repository's release workflow did not start, so this release carries the source archive only:

```
brew install amberframework/amber_cli/minecart
```

releases.body:
# Amber 2.0.0-beta.9

Amber 2.0.0-beta.9 adds what an application needs behind a proxy, adds a
security headers pipe, and ships its rules and guides with the framework, so a
language server and a coding assistant know them from the first edit.

## What changed

- **Trusted proxies (#1415).** `server.trusted_proxies` lists the proxies
  allowed to report a client's address and scheme. Amber resolves the client IP
  and decides HTTPS from those proxies only, reads one forwarding header family,
  and validates the setting before it starts serving.
- **UNIX socket listener (#1415).** An application can listen on a UNIX socket.
  The socket is created owner-and-group only, and a bind lock stops two
  processes from taking the same path.
- **`Amber::Pipe::SecurityHeaders` (#1422).** Sends `X-Content-Type-Options`,
  `X-Frame-Options`, `Content-Security-Policy` and `Referrer-Policy`, set through
  a typed `security_headers` section. Plug it into each browser, API and static
  pipeline. See the migration guide.
- **Rule pack for amber-lsp.** `.amber-lsp/packs/amber_v2.yml` checks for Grant
  models, the V2 security headers pipe, ECR views, the JSON perimeter, nil
  narrowing and output through `Log`. Each finding names the fix. Amber CLI 2.0.9
  or newer loads the pack with no setup and prints its guidance at the start of
  an assistant session.
- **API card for amber-lsp.** `amber-lsp lookup` now carries verified notes and
  compiler-error hints for Amber's controller, params, testing and job APIs.
  Public params and validator methods declare concrete return types.
- **Guides for coding assistants.** `minecart install` now copies every guide
  in `docs/guides/` into the application's `.claude/skills/`, with an index skill.

## Upgrade

New applications from Amber CLI 2.0.9 start on this release. For an existing one:

```yaml
dependencies:
  amber:
    github: amberframework/amber
    version: 2.0.0-beta.9
```

Then run `minecart update amber`. If the application runs behind a proxy, list
the proxy in `server.trusted_proxies`, because Amber reads forwarding headers from
listed proxies only. `HTTPS: on` is not read as a scheme signal.

An application that calls `Amber::Validators::Params` directly now sees declared
return types. Code that relied on the earlier inferred unions may need a change
at compile time.

## Release

The tag is `v2.0.0-beta.9`. The GitHub release for the tag states the tagged
commit hash, its tree hash, and the sha256 of the source tarball attached to
the release (`scripts/release_checksums.sh v2.0.0-beta.9` produces all three).
A file cannot carry its own tarball's hash, so they live in the release.

## Verify this release

```

Tree: f1e7332d02229aec58ab5303ade7fc6c9d14fcee

Tarball sha256: 89ee68dca35919b42a33a99422e50f1170114d6c7b3c3b461ec766000009e0b4
```

## Crystal Alpha with Incremental Compilation — 1.21.0-incremental-3

Parity release tracking upstream [Crystal 1.21.0](https://github.com/crystal-lang/crystal/releases/tag/1.21.0), plus the fork's incremental compilation, iOS/Android/watchOS target work, and `--shared` output mode.

### Highlights

- **The ECR helper ships precompiled (#13).** The Homebrew formula compiles the standard library's ECR helper (`ecr/process.cr`, behind `ECR.embed` and every Amber view) once at install time, into `share/agent-crystal/macro_run_seed`. A build whose cache has no helper runs that copy instead of compiling it, as long as it was built by the same compiler executable (MD5 of the executable) from unchanged standard-library files (timestamps plus an MD5 of every file) with the default macro run settings. Otherwise the compiler builds the helper as before. Source checkouts get the same with `make macro_run_seed`. On an Apple M4 Mac mini the default `amber new` app builds clean in 3.34 s instead of 4.38 s (debug, -24%) and 18.03 s instead of 18.91 s (`--release`, -5%), and a clean debug build peaks at 931 MiB instead of 1,097 MiB. Edited builds take the same time as before. The app it builds is the one a build with a warm macro run cache already produces; `--release` executables are byte-identical.
- **dsymutil is opt-in for unoptimized builds on macOS (#14).** `crystal build` without `--release` or `-O1`..`-O3` no longer runs `dsymutil` after linking. That saves 0.10 s on a clean debug build and 0.13 s after an edit on the same machine. The binary is unchanged; what changes is that exception backtraces of such a build show method names without file and line numbers, because the runtime reads them from `<output>.dwarf`. `--dsymutil` brings it back for one build, `--no-dsymutil` skips it anywhere, and `crystal run`, `spec`, `eval`, `play` and `watch --run` keep running it by default. lldb still finds the debug information through the object files in the compiler cache.

Together, against 1.21.0-incremental-2 on the same machine: debug clean 4.38 s to 3.20 s (-27%), debug edited 2.81 s to 2.58 s (-8%), release clean 18.91 s to 18.18 s (-4%), release edited unchanged.

### Provenance

- Tag `v1.21.0-incremental-3`, commit `946e55e1b73050d0c2b620e8461295a6c60ba2ac`.
- `crystal-alpha-1.21.0-incremental-3.tar.gz` (attached, `git archive` of the tag): sha256 `e0c4d38b45dadecdd577bab885760f68a503e3926b7bd57a1dbe9527d1b39c9a`.
- GitHub source archive `https://github.com/crimson-knight/crystal/archive/refs/tags/v1.21.0-incremental-3.tar.gz` (the URL the Homebrew formula pins): sha256 `580a1220641da5cd6e0750a74f2dc58db55ae56048a2c2144dda37fc6b28d139`. Both archives hold the same file tree.

Install via Homebrew:
```bash
brew install crimson-knight/agent-crystal/agent-crystal
```

Or build from source:
```bash
git clone --branch v1.21.0-incremental-3 https://github.com/crimson-knight/crystal
cd crystal
LLVM_CONFIG=$(brew --prefix llvm@21)/bin/llvm-config make crystal macro_run_seed release=1
```

## Crystal Alpha with Incremental Compilation — 1.21.0-incremental-4

Parity release tracking upstream [Crystal 1.21.0](https://github.com/crystal-lang/crystal/releases/tag/1.21.0), plus the fork's incremental compilation, iOS/Android/watchOS target work, and `--shared` output mode. Includes everything in 1.21.0-incremental-3 (precompiled ECR helper, dsymutil opt-in for unoptimized builds).

### Highlights

- **`--release` builds emit machine code on 8 threads (`--release-units`).** An optimized single-module build is still optimized as one whole program, then split into parts that are emitted as separate object files in parallel and linked together. On an M4 Mac mini the reference Amber app builds 3.1 s faster in release mode (18.71 s to 15.61 s clean, -17 percent; 17.93 s to 14.78 s after an edit, -18 percent), with the same peak memory. The default is 8 parts, at most `--threads`; `--release-units 1` restores the single object file. Splitting applies to macOS and Linux hosts with LLVM 17 or later; cross-compilation, `--emit`, WebAssembly and Windows keep one object.
- **Same program, same symbol table.** The optimized program is the same before the split. The executable lists the same function symbols as a single-object build (reference app: 3,099,720 bytes against 3,098,680 at one part); Crystal method names are unchanged. On Linux the compiler runs `objcopy` after linking to drop the helper symbols the split adds.
- The compiler spec suite (13,646 examples on macOS, 13,645 on Linux) passes with the spec binaries built at one part and at eight; the standard library suite fails the same examples at both.

### Provenance

- Tag `v1.21.0-incremental-4`, commit `8c27cbfe397f41cf7f8ba35a8b03257ea4533025`.
- `crystal-alpha-1.21.0-incremental-4.tar.gz` (attached, `git archive` of the tag): sha256 `0727b080563e83936f51b3d868b39a8c238127e161abda4199b79a02f8b3fbde`.
- GitHub source archive `https://github.com/crimson-knight/crystal/archive/refs/tags/v1.21.0-incremental-4.tar.gz` (the URL the Homebrew formula pins): sha256 `ae00ac905491a2d762220a216d707443b76815fb23a9bbfc858947657eb5a25a`. Both archives hold the same file tree.

Install via Homebrew:
```bash
brew install crimson-knight/agent-crystal/agent-crystal
```

Or build from source:
```bash
git clone --branch v1.21.0-incremental-4 https://github.com/crimson-knight/crystal
cd crystal
LLVM_CONFIG=$(brew --prefix llvm@21)/bin/llvm-config make crystal macro_run_seed release=1
```

# Amber 2.0.0-beta.8

Amber 2.0.0-beta.8 compiles on every Crystal version its `shard.yml`
declares, starting at 1.20.0, and lets an application choose the cache
policy for the static files it serves.

## What changed

- **Builds on Crystal 1.20 (#1434).** Beta.7 did not compile on Crystal
  1.20.x (`no parameter named 'writable'`), although it declares
  `crystal: ">= 1.20.0"`. Both `IO::Memory` calls now pass the read-only
  flag positionally, and CI runs the full suite on Crystal 1.20.0 next to
  1.22.1 and crystal-alpha.
- **Static files follow the application's cache policy (#1435).**
  `Amber::Pipe::Static` keeps a `Cache-Control` that an earlier handler
  already set. An application with its own fingerprint scheme overrides
  `#cache_control` in a subclass; the hook runs only for a file the pipe
  serves:

  ```crystal
  class AppStatic < Amber::Pipe::Static
    SHORT_FINGERPRINT = /-[0-9a-f]{8}\.[^\/]+$/i

    protected def cache_control(request_path : String) : String
      return IMMUTABLE_CACHE_CONTROL if request_path.matches?(SHORT_FINGERPRINT)
      super
    end
  end
  ```

  Asset headers now go on GET and HEAD responses only.

## Upgrade

```yaml
dependencies:
  amber:
    github: amberframework/amber
    version: 2.0.0-beta.8
```

Then run `minecart update amber`. An application that re-applied its own
`Cache-Control` after `super` in an `apply_asset_headers` override can move
that policy into `#cache_control`.

Amber CLI 2.0.8 generates projects on `2.0.0-beta.7`; change `version:` to
`2.0.0-beta.8` after `amber new`.

## Release

The tag is `v2.0.0-beta.8`. The GitHub release for the tag states the tagged
commit hash, its tree hash, and the sha256 of the source tarball attached to
the release (`scripts/release_checksums.sh v2.0.0-beta.8` produces all three).
A file cannot carry its own tarball's hash, so they live in the release.

## Crystal Alpha with Incremental Compilation — 1.21.0-incremental-2

Parity release tracking upstream [Crystal 1.21.0](https://github.com/crystal-lang/crystal/releases/tag/1.21.0), plus the fork's incremental compilation, iOS/Android/watchOS target work, and `--shared` output mode.

### Highlights

- **Faster clean builds for apps that render ECR (#12).** `{{ run }}` macro programs, such as the ECR helper every Amber app uses, compile at `-O0` with one LLVM module per type instead of in release mode. On an Apple M4 Mac mini the default `amber new` app builds clean in 4.40 s instead of 6.76 s (debug, -35%) and 18.86 s instead of 20.98 s (`--release`, -10%). Builds with a warm cache take the same time as before. Macro run programs keep the `release` flag, so their output is unchanged.
- **Lower peak memory.** Each compilation unit releases its LLVM contexts and target machine as soon as its object file is written, debug info builders are released when their module is finished, and `LLVM::MemoryBuffer#dispose` now frees its buffer. A clean debug build of the same app peaks at 1,097 MiB instead of 1,976 MiB; a `--release` build peaks at 1,665 MiB (1,685 MiB before).

### Provenance

- Tag `v1.21.0-incremental-2`, commit `57c62c3f1b724d383c946391dbf5d090ee872949`.
- `crystal-alpha-1.21.0-incremental-2.tar.gz` (attached, `git archive` of the tag): sha256 `fae68ab8dddec49aa5ea5516476020d0bbaf3cba212f300b5a73565d0f6f6abf`.
- GitHub source archive `https://github.com/crimson-knight/crystal/archive/refs/tags/v1.21.0-incremental-2.tar.gz` (the URL the Homebrew formula pins): sha256 `354e8af7cae6f902f39d1c9d545b85e2fdcc32b8cca631f2d73fdc079888da7c`. Both archives hold the same file tree.

Install via Homebrew:

releases.body:
# Amber 2.0.0-beta.7

Amber 2.0.0-beta.7 makes the fixes that AgentC applications carried on a
fork part of Amber itself, so those applications can depend on an official
release again. It also routes `.md` paths to the routes that declare them,
bounds request parameter parsing, and reads credentials from a systemd-style
credentials directory.

## What changed

- **A path ending in an extension reaches the route that declares it
  (#1431).** Beta.6 added `.md` to the response extensions it removes before
  matching, so `/projects/7/insights/overview.md` was matched as
  `/projects/7/insights/overview` and could land on a later `get "/*"`
  catch-all. A route that spells the extension in its own path, such as
  `get "/projects/:project_id/insights/overview.md"` or
  `get "/guides/setup(.md)"`, now answers first. A path that no route
  declares still has its extension removed, so `/users/1.json` matches
  `/users/:id`. A route's request constraint is asked once per request,
  and a constraint that reads `request.params` sees that route's
  parameters.
- **The request body stays readable after Amber parses a form (#1429).** A
  controller behind the CSRF pipe can read `request.body` again; the bytes
  are handed back from the bounded parse. A multipart body is restored up
  to `params.max_multipart_restore_bytes` (8 MiB by default, `0` turns it
  off) when its `Content-Length` is declared and within that limit and
  `params.max_multipart_body_bytes`; any other multipart body stays drained.
- **Upload tempfiles are deleted when the request finishes (#1429).** To
  keep an upload, call `Amber::Router::File#move_to(path)` during the
  action, or `#retain!` to keep the tempfile at `#path` and delete it
  yourself, for example after a background job.
- **Custom config sections load as raw YAML (#1430).** Amber no longer
  deserializes a custom section through every `YAML::Serializable` type, so
  an application whose Grant models have UUID columns compiles with custom
  config again. `AppConfig#custom` reads a section as the requested type or
  returns its registered default; an unregistered key raises
  `Amber::Exceptions::ConfigurationError`.
- **Settings load at first use (#1424).** `require "amber"` no longer reads
  settings, so a section registered in `config/initializers` reads its YAML
  value, and `config/application.cr` can still set `Amber.path` and
  `Amber.env`. Amber colors its own log lines from `logging.colorize` and
  leaves the global `Colorize.enabled` flag alone.
- **Request parameters are bounded (#1419).** Counts, nesting depth, key
  and value sizes, body sizes, array indices and padding, multipart parts,
  uploads and WebSocket messages each have a limit in the new `params:`
  section of `config/environments/<env>.yml` (or `AMBER_PARAMS_<KEY>`). An
  HTTP request beyond a limit is answered with `400 Bad Request`; a
  WebSocket message over `max_websocket_message_bytes` (2 MiB) closes the
  connection with code 1009. The defaults and every limit are listed in
  `CHANGELOG.md`.
- **Credentials directory (#1423).** `Amber::Configuration.register_credentials`
  reads a systemd-style credentials directory, one file per credential, into
  a typed section. The application passes the directory, usually from
  `CREDENTIALS_DIRECTORY`, before settings load:

  ```crystal
  if credentials_directory = ENV["CREDENTIALS_DIRECTORY"]?
    Amber::Configuration.register_credentials(:credentials, AppCredentials, credentials_directory)
  else
    Amber::Configuration.register(:credentials, AppCredentials)
  end
  ```

  `AMBER_{SECTION}_{KEY}` overrides now reach registered custom sections.
- **A GREEN build (#1421):** no compiler warnings. The ecosystem agent
  context now names Micrate, Gemma and Mica (#1417).

## Fork fixes now in Amber

| Fix | Fork commit | Upstream |
|---|---|---|
| Restore the request body after form parsing | `8c71a57c` | #1429 |
| Delete upload tempfiles at request teardown | `0fbd8eba` | #1429 |
| Read custom config as raw YAML | `bc0d62c6` | #1430 |
| Answer 404 before checking a route's constraint when no route matches | `valid_route?` guard | already in Amber (`7224cb57`) |

An application can drop its fork pin and depend on this release.

## Upgrade

Change the version:

```yaml
dependencies:
  amber:
    github: amberframework/amber
    version: 2.0.0-beta.7
```

Then check three things:

- **Uploads you keep.** An action that keeps an uploaded file past the
  request calls `#move_to` or `#retain!`; otherwise the tempfile is gone
  when the response is sent.
- **Large requests.** A form, JSON body or upload larger than the defaults
  (8 MiB form and document bodies, 64 MiB files, 128 MiB multipart bodies)
  needs its limit raised in `params:`.
- **Custom config readers.** Code that called
  `Amber::Configuration.load_custom_from_yaml` reads sections with
  `Amber.settings.custom(:name, Type)` instead.

Beta.6 also stopped sending `Keep-Alive` response headers (`deb16f8e`); a
spec that expects them needs updating.

## Release

The tag is `v2.0.0-beta.7`. The GitHub release for the tag states the tagged
commit hash, its tree hash, and the sha256 of the source tarball attached to
the release (`scripts/release_checksums.sh v2.0.0-beta.7` produces all three).
A file cannot carry its own tarball's hash, so they live in the release.

## Verify this release

```
Commit: 21deeec92b9253e9fc7252f994fc3465da0ffd4f
Tree: d7af4f30415f80e633c49c2d1ff0c32ac6ac7c1a
Tarball: amber-2.0.0-beta.7.tar.gz (git archive --format=tar.gz --prefix=amber-2.0.0-beta.7/ 21deeec92b9253e9fc7252f994fc3465da0ffd4f)
Tarball sha256: 988a556bd1bf85b6b7e2a24cbe80559b558694ed1ec1333fa5164f7059a0bddb
```

releases.body:
# Amber 2.0.0-beta.6

Amber 2.0.0-beta.6 takes libxml2 out of every Amber V2 application. Until
this release, every V2 app linked libxml2, and with it liblzma, because the
schema layer could parse XML request bodies. XML is now opt-in, and the
opt-in is Mica, a pure-Crystal XML parser, so an application that accepts
XML still links no XML library.

## What changed

- **XML request bodies are opt-in (#1414).** The libxml2-backed
  `Amber::Schema::Parser::XMLParser` is removed. A request sent as
  `application/xml`, `text/xml` or any `+xml` type is answered with
  `415 Unsupported Media Type` unless the application registers a parser.
- **`ParserRegistry.register_body_parser` (#1414)** lets an application add
  a request body format with one call at boot. A parser that raises answers
  the request with `400 invalid_request_body`.
- **CI is pinned (#1420):** Crystal 1.22.1 tarballs checked by sha256,
  GitHub Actions by full commit SHA, the CircleCI image by digest,
  dependencies from a committed `shard.lock` with `--frozen`, and a second job
  that builds crystal-alpha from an exact commit and runs the suite on it.
- **Specs pass on Crystal 1.22 (#1418)**, which rejects the empty request
  resource and the malformed multipart fixture some specs used.

## Turning XML back on with Mica

Add Mica v0.1.0
([release](https://github.com/amberframework/mica/releases/tag/v0.1.0),
commit `6a4866e`) to `shard.yml`:

```yaml
dependencies:
  mica:
    github: amberframework/mica
    version: 0.1.0
```

Register it in `config/initializers/request_body_parsers.cr`, and make sure
`config/application.cr` loads the initializers (`require "./initializers/*"`;
applications generated by Amber CLI 2.0.6 load `config/*.cr` only):

```crystal
require "mica/xml/fields"

{"application/xml", "text/xml"}.each do |media_type|
  Amber::Schema::Parser::ParserRegistry.register_body_parser(media_type) do |body|
    Mica::XML::Fields.read(body)
  end
end
```

List the media types in the action's schema:

```crystal
class CreateSubscriberSchema < Amber::Schema::Definition
  content_type "application/json", "application/xml", "text/xml"
  field :email_address, String, required: true, format: "email"
end
```

`Mica::XML::Fields.read` turns an XML body into the same fields a JSON object
gives, so `<subscriber><email_address>ada@example.com</email_address></subscriber>`
and `{"email_address": "ada@example.com"}` validate the same way. It refuses a
DTD at the `<!DOCTYPE` (so no external entity, entity expansion or attribute
default reaches the fields), caps bodies at 1 MiB and nesting at 64 levels,
and charges every step of the read to a work budget.

## Measured

A sample Amber V2 + Grant + PostgreSQL application
(`examples/zero_link_app`), built as a static musl binary with
`--static --release --no-debug` in the official Crystal 1.22.1 Alpine image
(pinned by digest, linux/arm64), from an empty compiler cache, twice per variant. Before
is Amber 2.0.0-beta.5 with its built-in XML parser; after is this release
with Mica registered. Evidence, scripts and raw logs:
`examples/zero_link_app/evidence/`.

| | before (beta.5) | after (#1414 + Mica) |
|---|---|---|
| libxml2 objects linked | 108 | 0 |
| liblzma objects linked | 68 | 0 |
| zlib objects linked | 15 | 11 |
| static archives used | 12 | 10 |
| defined `xml*` / `lzma_*` / zlib symbols | 2,420 / 109 / 46 | 0 / 0 / 46 |
| `-l` flags | adds `-lxml2 -llzma` | neither |
| binary size | 29,600,248 bytes | 26,103,720 bytes (11.8% smaller) |
| binary size after `strip` | 11,169,352 bytes | 10,381,728 bytes (7.1% smaller) |
| dynamic libraries needed (`readelf -d`) | none (static PIE) | none (static PIE) |
| clean release build, 2 runs | 109.0 s, 119.0 s | 93.0 s, 81.0 s |

Both binaries are static: `readelf -d` lists no NEEDED entries and there is
no program interpreter. zlib stays linked because Grant
(`grant/encryption/compression.cr`) and asset_pipeline
(`asset_pipeline/static_assets.cr`) use the standard library's `Compress`;
Amber itself does not. The remaining archives are libc, libcrypto, libssl,
libgc, libgmp, libpcre2-8, libyaml, libz and the compiler's libgcc and
libgcc_eh.

Build times are reported, not claimed: in this Docker VM (4 CPUs) the same
beta.5 build ranged from 83 to 133 seconds across five clean builds, so two
runs per variant cannot separate a compile-time change from noise.

The after binary, run in an Alpine image with no libxml2 installed, answered
JSON, `application/xml` and `text/xml` bodies with 201 and wrote 3 rows; an
invalid email with 422; malformed XML with 400 and its position; an external
entity and a billion-laughs body with 400 at the `<!DOCTYPE` (byte 0); and
`application/xhtml+xml` with 415 (`results/after.smoke.txt`).

Measured on 2026-11-01 with Amber `b9d246ba` and Mica `2a4ab10`, now
`c11b6cc` after a history rewrite that left file contents identical. The
sample now pins Mica v0.1.0 (`6a4866e`; see `../shard.lock`).

## Upgrade

An application that accepted XML bodies through the schema API either moves
those endpoints to JSON or registers Mica as above. Everything else upgrades
by changing the version:

```yaml
dependencies:
  amber:
    github: amberframework/amber
    version: 2.0.0-beta.6
```

## Release

The tag is `v2.0.0-beta.6`. The GitHub release for the tag states the tagged
commit hash, its tree hash, and the sha256 of the source tarball attached to
the release (`scripts/release_checksums.sh v2.0.0-beta.6` produces all three).
A file cannot carry its own tarball's hash, so they live in the release.

## Verify this release

```
Commit: a61cb0e436d3cffbc1feb381187b03c25e45f743
Tree: aef5979f5a1beec1c825a05ef83d8942583b5e38
Tarball: amber-2.0.0-beta.6.tar.gz (git archive --format=tar.gz --prefix=amber-2.0.0-beta.6/ a61cb0e436d3cffbc1feb381187b03c25e45f743)
Tarball sha256: ec0e01f0da912fbc618782ff7b8e610d3414a4c26a6be8b6e6b335aeba388d24
```

releases.body:
Amber CLI 2.0.7 helps coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex write Crystal that compiles the first time, in Amber V2 apps, plain Crystal apps, and Crystal shards.

## Install or upgrade

```bash
HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 brew install amberframework/amber_cli/amber_cli
amber --version
amber-lsp --version
```

## What's new

- **`amber-lsp lookup 'Type.method'`** answers from your project's real code: its own source, every shard in `lib/`, and the Crystal standard library. It prints the signature, the resolved return type, where the method is defined, its doc comment, and notes from API cards. It falls back to stock `crystal` when `crystal-alpha` is not installed.
- **`amber-lsp hint`** reads compiler output and prints the fix for known mistakes.
- **`amber setup:agent`** connects Claude Code and Codex to `amber-lsp` in any Crystal project. It installs hooks that tell the agent to look methods up first, format each edited file, check Amber V2 rules in Amber apps, and build when the agent stops. Crystal edits are held back until `amber-lsp` is installed and checksum-verified.
- **`amber doctor`** reports the same readiness checks, agent trust, and index freshness, with a fix for each failure.
- **`amber-lsp --help`** documents every mode.
- **API cards**: libraries ship notes and error hints in `.amber-lsp/api/*.yml`. Grant, Amber, asset_pipeline, micrate, and gemma now include cards, and the Crystal card is bundled.
- **Minecart 2025.11.25.8** is the pinned dependency manager.

In a 40-task evaluation, requiring lookup raised first-try compile rates from 85.0% to 97.5% (Sonnet) and from 62.5% to 82.5% (Haiku).

See the [agent tooling guide](https://github.com/amberframework/amber_cli/blob/main/docs/guides/ai-assistants.md).

releases.body:
# Amber CLI 2.0.6

Amber CLI 2.0.6 is the coordinated generator release for Amber
`2.0.0-beta.5`. Fresh web applications now use the framework's automatically
enforced schema contracts instead of constructing and validating a second
schema object inside each controller action.

## Generate a complete web application

```bash
amber new pet_tracker --type web
cd pet_tracker
shards install
amber assets check
amber generate scaffold Pet name:string:required species:string:required adopted:bool
amber database migrate
crystal spec
amber watch
```

The generated project pins canonical Amber `2.0.0-beta.5`, uses ECR, Grant,
SQLite, Micrate, local front-end assets, and a manifest-backed asset pipeline.

## What changed

- Resource scaffolds bind `PetSchema` automatically to `create` and `update`
  and read typed request-local values with `validated_as(PetSchema)`.
- HTML form schemas declare URL-encoded input and return the generated ECR form
  with visible field errors and HTTP 422 when a well-formed request is invalid.
- Malformed or unsupported form bodies preserve the framework's explicit 400
  or 415 status instead of being flattened into a generic validation error.
- Preview API generators bind the same executable schema contract for JSON
  writes while retaining structured JSON failures.
- `amber generate schema` teaches the executable controller declaration as the
  primary application path; direct construction remains available for isolated
  schema unit tests.
- The Unix and Windows generated-app smoke harnesses can test an exact framework
  repository and commit during coordinated development, while normal and
  release CI now exercise the published beta emitted by the template.

## Upgrade compatibility

Amber's deprecated `params.validation` API remains functional. Existing Amber
applications can update the framework first, verify their current behavior,
and migrate validation one controller action at a time. CLI 2.0.6 changes new
generators; it does not force an existing application to regenerate its
controllers.

## Release proof

- 412 Amber CLI examples pass.
- Apple Silicon macOS and x86_64 Linux release-style binaries generate, build,
  migrate, run, and exercise the complete web application.
- Linux ARM64 and Windows x86_64 compile and run the generated web application
  in GitHub Actions.
- The Pet Tracker smoke proves invalid HTML form input returns one HTML
  document with status 422 and a visible field error before proving persisted
  create and PATCH update behavior.
- Fingerprinted CSS, JavaScript, SVG, and favicon responses retain integrity,
  MIME, immutable caching, URL rewriting, and gzip checks.

Windows remains a source-build compatibility path; this release publishes CLI
archives for Apple Silicon macOS, x86_64 Linux, and ARM64 Linux.
releases.name: Amber CLI 2.0.6

releases.body:
# Amber 2.0.0-beta.5

Amber 2.0.0-beta.5 turns the V2 schema API into a contract the framework
actually enforces. A controller declaration now owns request parsing,
validation, typed access, response validation, content negotiation, and
OpenAPI 3.1 output. The release also brings the optimized router and request
path onto the V2 release line.

## Upgrade compatibility comes first

The existing `params.validation` API still compiles and runs. It is deprecated
so new work can use executable controller schemas, but upgrading to beta.5 does
not require rewriting every controller. Applications can update Amber, run
their existing tests, and then migrate one action at a time.

Amber does not plan to remove the deprecated validator before a later V2 minor
such as 2.5. The exact removal release will be announced separately.

## Executable request and response contracts

- `schema :action, SchemaClass` enforces the declared request before the action
  runs.
- `validated_as(SchemaClass)` exposes request-local typed values without
  constructing and validating a second schema object.
- Request fields can come from bodies, paths, query strings, headers, and
  cookies.
- `response_schema` verifies the declared status, content type, and response
  shape before delivery.
- OpenAPI 3.1 operations are generated from the same contracts the application
  executes.
- Server-rendered controllers can override the schema-failure hook to return an
  ECR form with field errors and the correct 400, 415, or 422 status.

## JSON, CBOR, and authenticated COSE

Amber now supports JSON, XML, URL-encoded forms, multipart forms, and bounded
CBOR request parsing. COSE Encrypt0 adds authenticated ChaCha20-Poly1305
encryption in both directions: Amber decrypts and authenticates the inbound
request, applies its schema, and can authenticate and encrypt the response with
a fresh nonce.

The request boundary fails explicitly for malformed documents, unsupported
media, invalid values, unacceptable response formats, invalid declared
responses, and temporarily unavailable encryption configuration.

## Measured performance

The release candidate was tested on a DigitalOcean Basic one-shared-vCPU,
512-MB-class target with a separate load generator, 16 keep-alive connections,
and seven rotating 15-second repetitions per scenario:

| Complete HTTP request path | Median requests/second |
|---|---:|
| Generic JSON decode | 20,728 |
| Schema-validated JSON | 19,488 |
| Schema-validated CBOR | 21,742 |
| Authenticated COSE request and response | 14,443 |

All 7,974,608 retained requests returned HTTP 200. This is a synthetic
in-memory acknowledgement workload without a database, TLS termination,
external services, or HTML rendering. It measures framework, codec, and schema
cost under constrained hardware; it is not a capacity promise for an arbitrary
production application.

See
[`benchmarks/DIGITALOCEAN_SCHEMA_CONTRACT_ROUND27.md`](https://github.com/amberframework/amber/blob/76954f0e2edc10d568e7ffcea3faa94b2aa476d2/benchmarks/DIGITALOCEAN_SCHEMA_CONTRACT_ROUND27.md)
for the complete method, ranges, before-and-after comparison, and evidence
paths.

## Start a fresh web application

Amber CLI 2.0.6 is the coordinated generator release for this beta:

```bash
brew install amberframework/amber_cli/amber_cli
amber new pet_tracker --type web
cd pet_tracker
shards install
amber assets check
amber generate scaffold Pet name:string:required species:string:required adopted:bool
amber database migrate
crystal spec
amber watch
```

The generated application uses ECR, Grant, SQLite, Micrate, local front-end
assets, executable HTML form schemas, and Amber `2.0.0-beta.5`.

See the [beta installation guide](https://github.com/amberframework/amber/blob/v2.0.0-beta.5/docs/beta-installation.md),
[migration guide](https://github.com/amberframework/amber/blob/v2.0.0-beta.5/docs/migration-guide.md),
and [schema guide](https://github.com/amberframework/amber/blob/v2.0.0-beta.5/docs/guides/schema-api.md).

releases.body:
Amber 2.0.0-beta.4 connects the V2 web runtime to the deterministic asset compiler and closes the fresh-application path across macOS, Linux, Linux ARM64, and Windows CI.

The `beta` label applies to the Amber 2.0 release train. The supported surface is the ECR web application created by Amber CLI 2.0.5; native applications and authentication generators remain explicitly marked preview features.

### What ships

- Manifest-backed `asset_path`, stylesheet, JavaScript/import-map, image, and favicon helpers with Subresource Integrity metadata.
- Production manifest caching and development reload behavior.
- Immutable cache headers plus correct media type and content-length metadata for fingerprinted assets.
- Precompressed gzip negotiation, byte ranges, conditional requests, `HEAD`, and safe non-fingerprinted fallback behavior.
- `AMBER_DATABASE_URL` configuration with `DATABASE_URL` fallback for generated Grant applications.
- Windows-safe server startup: Amber no longer invokes Crystal's unimplemented Windows signal-trap API.
- Updated installation, migration, asset-helper, configuration, and release-contract documentation with exact file locations.

### Supported fresh web-app contract

The release-gated path covers generation, dependency installation, asset compilation and verification, Grant/SQLite/Micrate migrations, resource scaffolds, specs, production compilation, server startup, the generated homepage, and live database CRUD.

- macOS Apple Silicon: supported and release-gated.
- Linux x86_64: supported and release-gated.
- Linux ARM64: supported and release-gated.
- Windows x86_64: the generated application path is release-gated in CI; build the CLI from source because a standalone Windows archive is not published yet.

### Validation

- 2,350 framework examples passed with no failures.
- GitHub Actions passed on Linux and macOS; CircleCI passed.
- The Windows generated-app gate compiles and runs this exact framework revision through Amber CLI CI.

Use Amber CLI 2.0.5 to create a new web application. See `docs/beta-installation.md` and `docs/migration-guide.md` in the repository for the reproducible install and upgrade procedures.

Full change: #1407

releases.body:
Asset Pipeline 0.37.0 removes a major production gap for Amber V2 applications: static assets beyond CSS and JavaScript now participate in the same deterministic build contract.

### What ships

- Recursively fingerprints images, fonts, CSS, JavaScript, source maps, and other static files.
- Rewrites local CSS `url(...)` and `@import` references plus JavaScript imports, exports, dynamic imports, and source-map references to fingerprinted outputs.
- Records the full digest, Subresource Integrity value, media type, byte size, and precompressed gzip metadata in a deterministic manifest.
- Verifies the generated directory against that manifest before deployment.
- Safely prunes only outputs owned by the previous manifest and publishes the new manifest last.
- Rejects path traversal, escaping symlinks, missing local references, and other inputs that would make a production build incomplete.
- Uses Windows-safe file discovery and includes a dedicated Windows static-asset job alongside the Linux and macOS matrix.

### Upgrade

Set `asset_pipeline` to `~> 0.37.0`, run `shards update asset_pipeline`, then build and verify your assets before compiling the application:

```console
amber assets build --env production
amber assets check --env production
```

The Amber V2 web template and framework integration use this release directly.

### Validation

- 2,071 web examples passed; 66 pending; no failures.
- Crystal latest passed on Windows, Linux, and macOS.
- Crystal 1.10.1 passed on Linux and macOS.

Full change: #14

releases.body:
# Amber 2.0.0-beta.3

Amber 2.0.0-beta.3 is the framework release for the database-backed web
application that Amber CLI 2.0.4 generates by default. The supported path now
includes Grant models, SQLite, Micrate migrations, and complete HTML resource
scaffolds instead of stopping at a database-free homepage.

## What changed

- Schema controllers parse browser form bodies, including bodies already read
  by routing or CSRF protection.
- Background-job workers can steal queued work without corrupting request
  activity accounting.
- ECR view paths are normalized on Windows.
- The HTML/JSON `respond_with` behavior is documented with executable examples.

## Install and exercise persistence

Install Amber CLI 2.0.4, then generate and migrate a real resource:

```bash
brew install amberframework/amber_cli/amber_cli
amber new pet_tracker --type web
cd pet_tracker
shards install
amber generate scaffold Pet name:string:required species:string:required adopted:bool
amber database migrate
crystal spec
amber watch
```

Open <http://localhost:3000/pets>. The generated model lives at
`src/models/pet.cr`, its SQL migration is under `db/migrations/`, and its ECR
form partial is `src/views/pet/_form.ecr`.

Amber CLI 2.0.4 ships release archives for Apple Silicon macOS, x86_64 Linux,
and ARM64 Linux. Windows x86_64 generated web applications are compile-gated
in CI; build the CLI from source on Windows for this beta.

See the [beta installation guide](https://github.com/amberframework/amber/blob/v2.0.0-beta.3/docs/beta-installation.md)
and [V1 to V2 migration guide](https://github.com/amberframework/amber/blob/v2.0.0-beta.3/docs/migration-guide.md).

Please report framework issues at
<https://github.com/amberframework/amber/issues> and CLI/template/install issues
at <https://github.com/amberframework/amber_cli/issues>.

releases.body:
## BREAKING CHANGES

SafeHTML v1 changes `Components::Component#render` from a plain `String` contract to `Components::SafeHTML`. Components and callers that treat rendered markup as an unrestricted string must migrate. This is a breaking 0.x minor release.

The release also enforces unsafe HTML sinks at construction and render time: inline `on*` handlers are banned, URL-bearing attributes require `SafeURL` validation, raw style/script and document-valued bodies use typed doors, malformed attribute names are rejected, and direct mutable-attribute bypasses are revalidated before bytes are emitted.

Migration references:

- [Output contract](https://github.com/amberframework/asset_pipeline/blob/v0.36.0/docs/SAFE_HTML_V1.md#2-the-contract)
- [Bans and typed safety doors](https://github.com/amberframework/asset_pipeline/blob/v0.36.0/docs/SAFE_HTML_V1.md#3-the-bans)
- [`raw()` policy](https://github.com/amberframework/asset_pipeline/blob/v0.36.0/docs/SAFE_HTML_V1.md#4-the-raw-policy)
- [Component migration guide](https://github.com/amberframework/asset_pipeline/blob/v0.36.0/docs/SAFE_HTML_V1.md#5-migration-guide-for-components)
- [Explicit v1 exclusions](https://github.com/amberframework/asset_pipeline/blob/v0.36.0/docs/SAFE_HTML_V1.md#6-whats-out-of-scope-for-v1-and-why)

## Included

- `SafeHTML` output type and `SafeBuffer` construction path.
- `SafeURL`, `SafeStyle`, `SafeSrcSet`, and typed APIs for compound/document sinks.
- A single render-time attribute-validation authority covering alternate mutation paths.
- Adversarial and falsifiability specs for URL, attribute-name, script, style, iframe `srcdoc`, SVG foreign-content, object `data`, and `formaction` cases.
- DataTable migration exemplar and the complete SafeHTML v1 contract/migration document.
- Shard version `0.36.0`, with the complete 12-commit SafeHTML history preserved by merge.

Full changes: https://github.com/amberframework/asset_pipeline/compare/v0.35.0...v0.36.0

releases.body:
## Breaking compatibility note

This is a 0.x minor release and contains breaking generated-markup and selector changes compared with v0.34.0. The component output moves away from legacy Bootstrap-shaped classes toward the current `am-*` and `data-ap-*` contracts. Consumers that assert exact markup or depend on old selectors must update when upgrading.

## The original fixes

- Publishes the accumulated Phase 10 line through the pre-SafeHTML boundary.
- Delivers the cross-platform UI and renderer work, design-system components, asset-pipeline updates, native bridges, documentation, and validation infrastructure from that line.
- Sets the shard version to 0.35.0 and corrects stale pre-SafeHTML web expectations.
- Preserves the full development history through a merge commit.

SafeHTML v1 and its additional breaking output contract are intentionally excluded; they follow separately in v0.36.0.

Full changes: https://github.com/amberframework/asset_pipeline/compare/v0.34.0...v0.35.0

## Ashard 2025.11.25.4

Ashard is the public name for this
[Crystal Shards](https://github.com/crystal-lang/shards)-compatible fork.
The current release artifacts and package names still ship as
`shards-alpha` during the transition.

### Alpha Features
- **AI docs distribution**: `shards install` copies AI docs from dependencies
- **SBOM generation**: `shards sbom` produces SPDX 2.3 / CycloneDX 1.6 JSON
- **MCP server distribution**: Dependencies can ship MCP server configs
- **Docs theming**: `shards docs` with CSS theming and AI assistant buttons
- **Postinstall tracking**: Version-aware script execution

### Install via Homebrew
```
brew tap crimson-knight/tap
brew install shards-alpha
```

### Documentation
[https://crimson-knight.github.io/shards](https://crimson-knight.github.io/shards)

### Install from binary
Download the archive for your platform and extract `shards-alpha` to your PATH.

